items.quote: calculate : f (0) , f (1), and f (2) what do you notice?
items.text: if $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ where $f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2x$ is a polynomial function of third degree in X. calculate: $f(0)$, $f(1)$, and $f(2)$. What do you notice?
items.notes: Single unnumbered Think and Discuss prompt.

items.quote: We notice that : f (0) = 0 , f (1) = 0 , f (2) = 0
So 0 , 1 and 2 are called the set of zeroes of the function.
items.claim: 0, 1 and 2 are called the set of zeroes of the function.

items.quote: the set of zeroes of the function f and its denoted by the sumbol Z (f).
items.claim: If $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a polynomial in x, then the set of values of x which makes $f(x)=0$ is called the set of zeroes of the function f and is denoted by the symbol $Z(f)$.

items.quote: Z (f) is the solution set of the equation f (x) = 0
items.claim: Z(f) is the solution set of the equation f(x) = 0.

items.quote: to get the zeros of the function f, put f(x) = 0 and solve
items.claim: To get the zeros of the function f, put f(x) = 0 and solve the resulting equation to find the set of values of x.
